depends_on: lib OpenProblemsLib.ShortIntervalPrimes (prime in (x, 1.21x] for x >= 25, Chebyshev 1852, proved in Lean)
notes: True: 2^n is a sum of n distinct primes for n >= 6, so a(n) = 2^n. Lean proof (2026-11-07) of A102237_main: a102237 n = 2^n for n >= 6, a102237 defined as in the entry. Induction on the number k of odd primes: W(k, L, U, M) (every N = k mod 2 in [L, U] is a sum of k distinct odd primes <= M) with M >= 25 and 0.42 M <= 1.21 (U - L) gives W(k+1, L + 1.21 M, U + 2M/1.21, 2M), adding a prime from (b, 1.21 b], b = max(N - U, M). Bases at k = 6: even N in [62, 152] with primes <= 39 and in [62, 374] with primes <= 78 (kernel tables); they cover 2^n (n even) and 2^n - 2 (n odd, plus 2). The prime bound is the library theorem exists_prime_Ioc_mul (Chebyshev psi bounds adapted from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd plus 85 Pratt-certified primes). Replaces the earlier Dusart-based induction. Outside Lean: none.

sources.cite: P. Dusart, Estimates of some functions over primes without R.H., arXiv:1002.0442 (2010), Prop. 6.8
